title: Output handling: escaping by context (HTML, attribute, JavaScript, URL)

videos.script: A patient writes her nickname with quotation marks in it. Nothing wrong with that. {{nickname}} On the profile page, the nickname goes into four places. A heading. A form field. A link. A script. {{four}} Each place has its own reader, and each reader has its own special characters. {{readers}} A quotation mark ends an attribute. An ampersand starts a new parameter in a link. A closing script tag ends the script, wherever it sits. {{special}} So there is no single escape function. There is one encoding per place. {{one}} A template engine does the commonest one for you, by default. The others you choose on purpose. {{template}} Today you write six tests, one per context, watch them fail against a page built with f-strings, and pass against a template. {{tests}}
